units.function: Mocked issue PATCH route tests for authoritative field-change responses and asynchronous activity projections for blockers, workspaces, Run handoffs and execution-policy participants.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest -> monolithic issue route -> mocked issue/access/activity/heartbeat/routine services plus partially real best-effort integrations; audit calls are observed after HTTP success.
units.keyDataModels: Issue before/after receipt, blocker relations, workspace selection, successful-Run handoff activity and review/approval stage participants typed as human or Agent.
units.lifecycle: Authorize fixed board actor -> mutate Issue -> return full/minimal change receipt -> asynchronously enrich and log projections -> best-effort integration/cleanup side effects may fail after success.
units.testAssessment: Sandboxed run failed 10/10 on prohibited TCP bind; approved unsandboxed run passed 10/10 while emitting external-sync and sandbox-cleanup warnings. Receipt shape is well tested, but authorization, transactionality, idempotency and side-effect failure containment are not.
units.designRationale: Give API clients compact authoritative before/after mutation feedback and produce readable operational activity for relationship, workspace, handoff and policy changes without blocking the main Issue update.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs exact, attributable responsibility evidence for Work, approval and handoff mutations while allowing optional UI/integration projections to fail independently.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT minimal/full change receipts, no-op omission, canonical relation diffs and explicit human/Agent participant changes. Add content digests and governed evidence references, action-specific authority, policy version, accountable human, idempotency and a transactional outbox for mandatory responsibility records; keep optional integrations separately best-effort.
units.responsibilityConflict: Activity is asserted after a successful response and the green run tolerates downstream warnings, so it cannot prove atomic evidence. Handoff resolution and approver changes lack accountable-human authority, exact contract/action digest and separation-of-duties assertions.

units.securityFindings: HIGH audit-atomicity gap: activity is not proven committed with mutation. HIGH authorization gap: only a fixed same-company human actor is exercised. HIGH approval-governance gap: policy participant changes lack authority/separation/version assertions. HIGH evidence gap: long text is truncated without digest/full evidence reference. MEDIUM side-effect observability gap: integration and lease cleanup warnings do not fail tests. MEDIUM privacy gap: readable workspace titles/IDs enter activity without classification tests.
